description: Convert a Docker image to an executable

summary.one_liner: docker2exe is a Go tool that packages a Docker image into a standalone executable so the image can be run on another machine with a single command.
summary.what_it_does: The tool takes a Docker image name (for example alpine:3.9) and generates executables for several platforms, written to a dist directory. Running a generated executable with arguments runs a command inside that image (for example, cat /etc/alpine-release). When the executable runs, it checks whether the required image exists locally and pulls it with docker pull if missing. An optional embed mode saves the image as a gzipped tarball and bakes it into the executable, so the executable can load it with docker load when the image is absent. The README says small images work well with embedding, and gives an example executable under 10MB. Building requires Docker, Go and gzip; running requires only Docker.
use_cases: share a dockerized tool with someone who lacks it installed
distribute a command-line program packaged as a container
run a container image as a single binary
ship an offline-capable docker image inside an executable
cross-compile container wrappers for macOS, Linux and Windows
how_to_run: Download a binary from the releases page
notable: Produces executables for darwin, linux and windows from one command
Embed mode bakes a gzipped docker save tarball into the executable for offline loading
Generated binaries pull the image on first run if it is missing
Arguments passed to the generated executable are run inside the container
caveats: Both the building device and the executing device need Docker installed
Building requires Go and gzip in addition to Docker
Embedding is described as suited to small images; large images produce large executables
README does not state a license
